steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Stir together the chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, brown sugar, and meat tenderizer. Rub the spice mixture generously all over the brisket. Place the meat on a baking sheet with the fat layer up.

Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour; remove from oven, and lower the oven temperature to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Mix soy sauce with water in a bowl, and pour the liquid into a roasting pan. Transfer the brisket into the roasting pan. Sprinkle the meat with the crushed pineapple.
Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil, return to oven, and bake for 3 more hours. Cool for 30 minutes before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Nana Lara's Brisket
raw_recipe.description: A flavorful but chewy cut like a brisket needs a long, slow trip through the oven to break down the connective tissue and release the beefy goodness. A spice rub and a bit of crushed pineapple add their spicy, sweet flavors to the meat.
raw_recipe.name: Nana Lara's Brisket

review.reviewBody: Will make again. From my husband, "mommy's brisket is good!" It was delicious - even without the pinneaples (I didn't have any on hand).

Didn't have meat tenderizer, instead added 1 Tbsp McCormick Season-All & 1 Tbsp Goya Adobo; increased brown sugar (light) to 1-1/2 Tbsp - all on a 5# fresh brisket. Also- crushed pineapple used was a 20 oz. can. After the 1 hr @ 350, I reduced heat to 275 for 3-1/2 hrs. OMG - sooooo tender & delicious.!!
Huge hit. I left the meat tenderizer out and cooked it on a rack on a roasting pan at 300 degrees for the entire time. It was excellent! I did not know brisket was this easy!
I make this recipe all the time and every time everyone loves it!! I make a couple modifications, I do not use pineapple, and I lower the water amount a little and add a bottle of liquid smoke.

Excellent flavor! I only had a 1.5 lb brisket so I quartered the recipe (and also omitted the pineapple). But I used the baking directions from the "Easy Bake Brisket" recipe because it seemed easier. I would highly recommend this ingredient combination though!

Definitely deserves the 5 star rating! So juicy, so tender, so easy and loaded with flavor. I followed the recipe exactly, omitting the pineapple because I didn't have any on hand but it didn't hinder the flavor at all. I will make this again and again.
This is amazing!!! My family loves it!

I just didn’t find this recipe to be very good. I used grass-fed and finished brisket and followed the recipe. It was just ok. I was thinking maybe it’s because I am from Texas and maybe I just think of brisket as needing smoke, but no, it just wasn’t amazing.

This was fantastic!!! I changed a bunch of stuff, royally messed it up, and even with all my mistakes it still turned out awesome. I used a rib eye roast, I didn't have onion powder so I doubled the garlic powder, I didn't have meat tenderizer so I used a tbsp of salt, I didn't have canned pineapple so I used fresh pineapple, and then to top it off I cooked it waaaay too long. STILL AWESOME. Can't go wrong with this recipe, or even your own random interpretation of this recipe.
Awesome. If you don't like heat then hold off to half tablespoon. But very tender and the best brisket I EVER made.
I don't think I'll ever cook brisket another way. This was absolutely amazing. #noleftovers
I prepared it as instructed except for the fact that I used the ancho chili powder I had since I did not have any regular chili powder. It was a huge hit. My wife even high fived me after I made it.

BRISKET SHOWDOWN! 

Nana Lara's Brisket vs. Wine-Braised Beef Brisket (both 5 star ratings but which did we like better?)


Used the cooking method from this recipe for both briskets. Both were tender. Flavor wise - Nana Lara's is the winner in our family. The rub makes a huge difference which encrusts the brisket. The soy/pineapple combo brings a yummy flavor.
This was amazing. Flavor was incredible. Simple and delicious. Will maybe try in a crock pot to save on time.

I found this recipe when searching for something to do with a brisket I had. My family loved!!! We now make it for every special occasion and big get together. Would definitely say give it a try. My dad even likes it and he doesn't care for brisket.
